problem: The sentence 'Only a few universities teach this chapter' is inaccurate: invertible maps and isomorphisms are core material in almost every first linear algebra syllabus, so a student may skip it thinking it is optional.
fix: Delete that sentence, or say: 'This is standard material in first courses, sometimes called non-singular transformations.'

problem: The trap does not say which way the dimensions differ. With dim V > dim W a map can never be one-to-one, so a student may wrongly read the bullet as saying one-to-one is possible whenever dim V ≠ dim W.
fix: 'If dim V < dim W, a map can be one-to-one but never onto; if dim V > dim W, it can be onto but never one-to-one. Only dim V = dim W allows both. Check dimensions before calling a map invertible.'

problem: 'It may still map some nonzero vector to zero' is too weak. When det A = 0, a nonzero vector is always sent to zero, and that non-trivial kernel is exactly why the map fails to be invertible.
fix: 'A square matrix with determinant 0 is not invertible. It always sends some nonzero vector to zero, so it is not one-to-one.'
